prompt: A printable US Letter portrait page (8.5 by 11 inches) for a kids' pretend-play game, drawn flat and straight-on and filling the whole image: the page itself, not a photo or mockup of paper. Plain white paper with a clean white margin of about half an inch on every side where nothing is drawn, so it prints on a home printer. The game is "Pirate Treasure Hunt". Art style for the whole kit: bright, friendly flat vector cartoon like a modern kids' picture-book app: bold clean dark purple outlines, flat cheerful fills in coral red, sunny yellow, lime green, sky blue, deep purple and cream, soft rounded shapes, no gradients, no shading texture, no photo effects, lots of white paper. Ink-friendly: color sits on white, no full-page dark background. Draw ONE treasure map that fills the page inside the margin: an old paper scroll with curled ends, a picture-book map of a sunny little island seen from above, a winding dashed path that visits 4 stops in order, each stop a big simple landmark drawing with its name on a little flag or plaque beside it: "Big Rock", "Palm Tree", "Cave", "Treasure". The last stop has a big red X. A friendly compass rose with no letters. Title across the top on a ribbon: "Treasure Map". The ONLY words on the page, spelled exactly letter for letter: "Treasure Map", "Big Rock", "Palm Tree", "Cave", "Treasure". Big, clear, rounded print letters, easy for a 5-year-old to read, dark on a light background, never curved along a path, never tiny. No other words, letters, numbers or signatures anywhere. Kid-friendly and gentle, for ages 4 to 8: no guns, no knives, no real weapons (a toy sword is fine), no blood, nothing scary, no real people, no brands, no logos.
